steps.explanationAfterStep: One concerted step through a six-membered ring of atoms, like a pericyclic reaction: CO₂ leaves and the enol of the ketone forms. Only acids with a C=O β to the carboxyl group lose CO₂ this easily: the ketone is the electron sink.
H₃O⁺ protonates the enol on carbon. This is acid-catalysed enolisation run backwards.
The ketone is back, with one CO₂H gone. The second CO₂H is still β to the same ketone.
The same six-membered ring of atoms on the other side. The enol double bond lies inside the six-membered ring, away from the bridgehead carbons, so the bicycle has no trouble holding it.
H₃O⁺ protonates the second enol on carbon.
Tropinone, as its hydrochloride in the acid. Adding base frees the amine. The two CO₂H groups were activating groups: they made the enol and were then removed, a job acetone alone does badly.

title: Tropinone: losing two CO₂
subtitle: Both β-keto acid groups leave as CO₂ through six-membered rings, giving tropinone
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 26 (the Mannich reaction and Robinson's tropinone synthesis)
R. Robinson, A synthesis of tropinone, J. Chem. Soc., Trans., 1917, 111, 762–768

monoacid.caption: the β-keto monoacid + CO₂ + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: A β-keto acid loses CO₂ on heating through a six-membered ring of atoms: the acid proton, its oxygen, the carboxyl carbon, the α-carbon, the ketone carbon and the ketone oxygen.
Three arrows round that ring, all at once: the ketone oxygen takes the acid proton, the O–H pair becomes a C=O π bond in CO₂, and the C–C bond to the carboxyl carbon becomes a C=C π bond of an enol.
Ketone C=O π bond → new O–H bond to the acid proton; that acid O–H bond → a C=O π bond in the leaving carboxyl; the C–C bond to the carboxyl carbon → a C=C π bond to the ketone carbon.
monoacid.learnerPrompt: The second carboxyl group is still β to the ketone. Decarboxylate it the same way.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Breaking the C–C bond onto carbon alone would leave a carbanion. Let the electrons flow into the ketone as its oxygen takes the acid proton.
The carboxyl group leaves as neutral CO₂: the C–C bond pair stays behind as the C=C π bond of the enol.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the ketone oxygen takes the acid proton. Two more arrows round the ring.

reactants.caption: tropinone-2,4-dicarboxylic acid (as its hydrochloride) + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: A β-keto acid loses CO₂ on heating through a six-membered ring of atoms: the acid proton, its oxygen, the carboxyl carbon, the α-carbon, the ketone carbon and the ketone oxygen.
Three arrows round that ring, all at once: the ketone oxygen takes the acid proton, the O–H pair becomes a C=O π bond in CO₂, and the C–C bond to the carboxyl carbon becomes a C=C π bond of an enol.
Ketone C=O π bond → new O–H bond to the acid proton; that acid O–H bond → a C=O π bond in the leaving carboxyl; the C–C bond to the carboxyl carbon → a C=C π bond to the ketone carbon.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Heat: one carboxyl group leaves as CO₂ through a six-membered ring of atoms.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Breaking the C–C bond onto carbon alone would leave a carbanion. In a β-keto acid the electrons flow on into the ketone, and the ketone oxygen takes the acid proton at the same time.
H₃O⁺ is an acid, not a base. In hot acid the carboxyl group keeps its proton and passes it to the ketone oxygen inside the molecule.
The carboxyl group leaves as neutral CO₂, taking no extra electrons: the C–C bond pair stays behind and becomes the C=C π bond of the enol.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the ketone oxygen takes the acid proton. Now carry the electrons on round the ring: two more arrows.
Good. The carboxyl carbon now has five bonds: its bond to the ring carbon must break, towards the ketone carbon.

first-enol.caption: the enol + CO₂ + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: An enol in acid turns back into the ketone. Which atom of the enol is protonated: oxygen or carbon?
The enol carbon takes a proton from H₃O⁺, pushed by the oxygen lone pair; the positive charge ends on the oxygen. Three arrows.
Enol oxygen lone pair → a C=O π bond; C=C π bond → new C–H bond to the proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond of H₃O⁺ → a lone pair on water's oxygen.
first-enol.learnerPrompt: The enol turns back into the ketone: protonate its carbon with H₃O⁺.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The enol cannot pass its own OH proton across to carbon. Protons move through the solvent: take one from H₃O⁺.
Protonating the enol oxygen leads nowhere. Protonate the enol carbon, pushed by the oxygen lone pair.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right bonds, but this leaves a positive carbon. Push the enol oxygen lone pair in to stabilise it.

second-enol.caption: the second enol + two CO₂ + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: An enol in acid turns back into the ketone. Which atom of the enol is protonated: oxygen or carbon?
The enol carbon takes a proton from H₃O⁺, pushed by the oxygen lone pair; the positive charge ends on the oxygen. Three arrows.
Enol oxygen lone pair → a C=O π bond; C=C π bond → new C–H bond to the proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond of H₃O⁺ → a lone pair on water's oxygen.
second-enol.learnerPrompt: Protonate the enol carbon with H₃O⁺ once more.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The enol cannot pass its own OH proton across to carbon. Protons move through the solvent: take one from H₃O⁺.
Protonating the enol oxygen leads nowhere. Protonate the enol carbon, pushed by the oxygen lone pair.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right bonds, but this leaves a positive carbon. Push the enol oxygen lone pair in.

first-protonated-ketone.caption: the protonated ketone + water
hintTiers: The ketone is protonated. Which base is around?
Water takes the proton on the positive oxygen. Two arrows.
Water lone pair → new O–H bond to the proton on the carbonyl oxygen; that O–H bond → a lone pair on that oxygen.
first-protonated-ketone.learnerPrompt: Water takes the proton off the carbonyl oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Water can add to a protonated ketone, but that only gives a hydrate. Remove the proton instead.
Taking the proton back off carbon just re-forms the enol. Remove the proton on oxygen.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: water takes the proton. Where does the O–H bonding pair go?

Water lone pair → new O–H bond to the proton on the carbonyl oxygen; that O–H bond → a lone pair on that oxygen.

mechanismSummary: Heating tropinone-2,4-dicarboxylic acid in aqueous HCl removes both carboxyl groups. Each one leaves as CO₂ in a concerted step through a six-membered ring of atoms: the ketone oxygen takes the acid proton, and the C–C bond to the carboxyl carbon becomes the C=C of an enol. H₃O⁺ protonates the enol on carbon and water removes the proton from oxygen, giving back the ketone. Twice over, this gives tropinone, isolated as its hydrochloride; the nitrogen stays protonated throughout and takes no part. The decarboxylations destroy the two stereocentres next to the ketone; tropinone itself is a symmetrical (meso) bicycle, and the app does not check stereochemistry yet.
